sheet-9999997-1.description: The main map of the single Whitehouse Station sheet covers the village along Main Street, from Nelson Street at the top to Kline Boulevard at the bottom, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet, lined with dwellings, stores, a tin shop and filling stations. Creamery Street runs parallel to it on the west from Nelson Street to Railroad Avenue, with the Cush-Mont Dairy of George N. Clark at its south end. Whitehouse Avenue leaves Main Street towards the east past dwellings, coops, a lumber yard and lumber store, a bakery and the Whitehouse Consolidated School at the right edge. Railroad Avenue runs along the north side of the Central Railroad of New Jersey on both sides of Main Street, with the Union Hotel, an auto repair shop, gasoline tanks, a builders' supply warehouse and the railroad signal tower; west of the tracks it bends south. South of the railroad are the depot, the 50,000 gallon water tank, the freight house, W. E. Lang's hay and feed store, the post office, a bank, a printing office and a drug store, then High Street and Skillman Alley to the west and the fire department further down Main Street. The lower part of the sheet is thinly built, with Kline Boulevard and the Rose Villa house at the bottom right. Notes on the fire department and water facilities, a location map of New Jersey, the key and the title cartouche are printed in blank areas of the sheet; small insets at the top and right show places outside the main map.
notes: Creamery Street is James Street today.
Railroad Avenue east of Main Street is Somerset Street today; west of Main Street it keeps the name Railroad Avenue.
Skillman Alley, drawn 12 ft wide, is the east end of today's High Street; its junction with Main Street was hand-picked.
The junction of Main Street and Whitehouse Avenue was hand-picked (the detector locked onto a line 65 ft north).
The two James Street (Creamery) junctions and Kline Boulevard keep residuals of about 4 m: the modern streets or the drawing are slightly off.

Single sheet, June 1928, 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left. Main map (part 1): Main Street, Nelson, Creamery (now James Street), Railroad Avenue (east of Main now Somerset Street), Whitehouse Avenue, High Street and Skillman Alley, Kline Boulevard, Central Railroad of New Jersey. Insets: part 2 State Highway and Main Street (north end of Main Street at US 22 / Old Hwy 28); part 3 the village of Whitehouse along the State Highway (Old Hwy 28, east of the reference box first fetched; box extended to -74.723); part 4 Whitehouse Station Reformed Church on Main Street; part 5 Central R.R. of N.J. pumping station on the North Rockaway River (not placed); part 6 R. C. Church of Our Lady of Lourdes, Main Street and Shampanore Road (taken as Pulaski Road). A location map of New Jersey, notes on fire department and water facilities, the key and the cartouche are masked out.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Central R.R. of N.J. pumping station on the North Rockaway River, 1/2 mile north-west of the post office (no street drawn; only the river and the building; needs step 6b: the pumping station site on Rockaway Creek, from a parcel corner or the building).

sheet-9999997-2.description: A small inset in the upper left corner of the sheet shows where Main Street meets the State Highway north of Whitehouse Station village. The highway, labelled State Highway or Main Street and 60 ft wide, crosses the top of the inset; Main Street, 45 ft wide, comes up from the lower left, with a triangular island where it joins the highway. Buildings drawn are a store with gasoline tanks on the north side of the highway, an auto repair shop with gasoline pumps at the corner, a storage building and a few dwellings, in blocks numbered 28, 29 and 30. Notes give the distances of 1 1/2 miles east along the highway to the M. E. church (on the inset of Whitehouse to the right) and 1/4 mile down Main Street to the Reformed church. The inset has its own north arrow and is drawn at the sheet's scale of 100 ft to an inch.
notes: Main is Main Street today; the State Highway is Old Hwy 28 to the east and US 22 to the west of the junction, which is one node in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one hand-picked point at the junction with the sheet's scale and a rotation estimated from the direction of Main Street (about 20 degrees): low confidence.

sheet-9999997-3.description: A strip across the top of the sheet shows the village of Whitehouse, east of Whitehouse Station, along the State Highway or Main Street, which runs straight across the strip. The north side holds dwellings and stores numbered 101 to 125, the M. E. church (heated by steam, lit by electricity) with its rectory, the fire department and a blacksmith shop; the south side holds dwellings numbered 126 to 146 and outbuildings, in blocks 31, 32 and 33. A road leaves the highway towards the south in the middle of the strip. The strip is drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow; a note at its west end gives 1 1/2 miles to the State Highway and Main Street.
notes: The State Highway here is Old Hwy 28 in OpenStreetMap; US 22 now bypasses the village to the south.

The road south from the highway is taken to be today's Fire Lane (the fire department stands opposite it); placed from its detected junction with Old Hwy 28 with the sheet's scale and the rotation of its measured lines: low confidence.
Modern Old Hwy 28 bends south-east of the road junction while the drawn highway is straight; at the east end of the strip the two are about 35 m apart, so the placement is least certain there.

sheet-9999997-4.description: An inset to the right of the main map shows the Whitehouse Station Reformed Church on Main Street north of the village, between Main Street (50 ft wide) and a road (30 ft wide) that converge towards the south. The church is a stone building of two stories heated by steam and lit by electricity, with a long shed behind it, in block 27; nothing else is drawn. Notes along Main Street give 1/4 mile north to the State Highway and 475 ft south to Nelson Street. The inset is drawn at the sheet's scale of 100 ft to an inch.
notes: Main is Main Street today.

No junction is drawn: placed from one point on the centre of Main Street at the foot of the inset, set 475 ft (145 m) north of the Nelson Street junction along modern Main Street as the note says, with the sheet's scale and a rotation from the direction of Main Street: low confidence.

sheet-9999997-6.description: An inset in the lower right of the sheet shows the Roman Catholic Church of Our Lady of Lourdes and its rectory on Main Street south of the village, at the corner of Shampanore Road. The church (heated by steam, lit by electricity) and the rectory stand in block 25 east of Main Street; block 24 on the west side has a dwelling, a small building marked as a store on its first floor and an outbuilding, and block 26 lies south of Shampanore Road. A note gives the distance of 1170 ft north along Main Street to Kline Boulevard. Main Street is 50 ft wide and Shampanore Road 35 ft. The inset has its own north arrow and is drawn at the sheet's scale of 100 ft to an inch.
notes: Shampanore Road is taken to be today's Pulaski Road, the first street meeting Main Street from the east about 370 m south of Kline Boulevard; the sheet's notes put it about 400 m south.
Placed from the detected Main Street / Pulaski Road junction with the sheet's scale and the rotation of its measured lines: low confidence.
